reason: The cited evidence only generally notes the room-temperature brittleness of RHEAs (E3) and mentions irradiation resistance in other alloy systems (E1), but provides no specific support for the claimed microstructural evolution, ductilization mechanism, or irradiation tolerance of Ti/Zr-modified NbMoTaW. Key premises rely on unsupported mechanistic assumptions.
premises: Minor HCP-stabilizing additions (Ti/Zr) to BCC NbMoTaW will produce a dual-phase BCC+HCP microstructure.
The HCP phase activates extra slip systems and enables transformation-induced toughening, improving room-temperature ductility.
The HCP phase enhances defect recombination under irradiation, improving irradiation tolerance.
The dominant BCC phase preserves the high-temperature strength of NbMoTaW up to 1600 °C.
The dual-phase alloy will show reduced helium blistering compared to single-phase NbMoTaW.
